title: Why is glass transparent? - Mark Miodownik
speaker: TED-Ed
zh: 【TED-Ed】玻璃為什麼是透明的？ ——馬克‧米歐多尼克（精選雙語跟讀教材）

cues.text: Take a look out your window, put on your glasses if you wear them.
cues.en: Take a look out your window, put on your glasses if you wear them.
cues.zh: 朝窗外看看， 如果你有眼鏡，把它戴上 你可能也需要一副望遠鏡

cues.text: You might want to grab a pair of binoculars, too, or a magnifying lens.
cues.en: You might want to grab a pair of binoculars, too, or a magnifying lens.
cues.zh: 你可能也需要一副望遠鏡 或是放大鏡 那麼，現在你看到了什麼？

cues.text: Now, what do you see?
cues.en: Now, what do you see?
cues.zh: 或是放大鏡 那麼，現在你看到了什麼？

cues.text: Well, whatever it is, it's not the multiple layers of glass
cues.en: Well, whatever it is, it's not the multiple layers of glass
cues.zh: 那麼，現在你看到了什麼？ 不論是什麼 你眼前出現的

cues.text: right in front of you.
cues.en: right in front of you.
cues.zh: 你眼前出現的 總不會是一層層的玻璃

cues.text: But have you ever wondered how something so solid can be so invisible?
cues.en: But have you ever wondered how something so solid can be so invisible?
cues.zh: 總不會是一層層的玻璃 你曾否想過 這麼堅固的東西 怎麼可能如此剔透？ 要了解其中原因

cues.text: To understand that, we have to understand what glass actually is,
cues.en: To understand that, we have to understand what glass actually is,
cues.zh: 要了解其中原因 我們得先了解玻璃究竟是什麼 以及它是從哪裡來的

cues.text: and where it comes from.
cues.en: and where it comes from.
cues.zh: 我們得先了解玻璃究竟是什麼 以及它是從哪裡來的

cues.text: It all begins in the Earth's crust, where the two most common elements are
cues.en: It all begins in the Earth's crust, where the two most common elements are
cues.zh: 這一切都得從地殼開始說起 組成地殼最主要的兩種成分是

cues.text: silicon and oxygen.
cues.en: silicon and oxygen.
cues.zh: 矽和氧

cues.text: These react together to form silicon dioxide, whose molecules arrange themselves
cues.en: These react together to form silicon dioxide, whose molecules arrange themselves
cues.zh: 矽和氧 這兩種成分經由 化學變化後形成二氧化矽 當中的分子排列 組成規則的晶體 也就是我們所知的石英

cues.text: into a regular crystalline form known as quartz.
cues.en: into a regular crystalline form known as quartz.
cues.zh: 組成規則的晶體 也就是我們所知的石英 石英在砂子裡很常見

cues.text: Quartz is commonly found in sand, where it often makes up most of the grains
cues.en: Quartz is commonly found in sand, where it often makes up most of the grains
cues.zh: 石英在砂子裡很常見 它是常見組成砂粒

cues.text: and is the main ingredient in most type of glass.
cues.en: and is the main ingredient in most type of glass.
cues.zh: 它是常見組成砂粒 以及大部分玻璃種類的主要成分 當然，你或許已經注意到

cues.text: Of course, you probably noticed that glass isn't made of multiple tiny bits of quartz,
cues.en: Of course, you probably noticed that glass isn't made of multiple tiny bits of quartz,
cues.zh: 當然，你或許已經注意到 玻璃並不是由許多 細小的石英顆粒組成的

cues.text: and for good reason.
cues.en: and for good reason.
cues.zh: 玻璃並不是由許多 細小的石英顆粒組成的 這背後有其道理在

cues.text: For one thing, the edges of the rigidly formed grains and smaller defects within the crystal structure
cues.en: For one thing, the edges of the rigidly formed grains and smaller defects within the crystal structure
cues.zh: 首先，當光線照射到砂粒粗糙的邊緣 以及晶體結構中的微小瑕疵時 會向四面八方反射分散

cues.text: reflect and disperse light that hits them.
cues.en: reflect and disperse light that hits them.
cues.zh: 會向四面八方反射分散

cues.text: But when the quartz is heated high enough the extra energy makes the molecules vibrate
cues.en: But when the quartz is heated high enough the extra energy makes the molecules vibrate
cues.zh: 但若石英加熱到一定溫度時 多餘的能量促使石英分子振動

cues.text: until they break the bonds holding them together and become a flowing liquid,
cues.en: until they break the bonds holding them together and become a flowing liquid,
cues.zh: 多餘的能量促使石英分子振動 直到打斷分子之間的鍵結 而變成流動的液體

cues.text: the same way that ice melts into water.
cues.en: the same way that ice melts into water.
cues.zh: 就如同冰溶化成為水一般 但不同於水的是，液態的二氧化矽

cues.text: Unlike water, though, liquid silicon dioxide does not reform into a crystal solid when it cools.
cues.en: Unlike water, though, liquid silicon dioxide does not reform into a crystal solid when it cools.
cues.zh: 就如同冰溶化成為水一般 但不同於水的是，液態的二氧化矽 冷卻後不會變回固態的晶體

cues.text: Instead, as the molecules lose energy, they are less and less able
cues.en: Instead, as the molecules lose energy, they are less and less able
cues.zh: 冷卻後不會變回固態的晶體 反之，當二氧化矽分子的能量減弱 他們越來越不可能

cues.text: to move into an ordered position, and the result is what is called an amorphous solid.
cues.en: to move into an ordered position, and the result is what is called an amorphous solid.
cues.zh: 他們越來越不可能 回復到規律整齊的排列 結果形成所謂的非晶態固體 具有液體般混亂結構的固體

cues.text: A solid material with the chaotic structure of a liquid,
cues.en: A solid material with the chaotic structure of a liquid,
cues.zh: 具有液體般混亂結構的固體 其中的分子可自由移動 填充任何的間隙

cues.text: which allows the molecules to freely fill in any gaps.
cues.en: which allows the molecules to freely fill in any gaps.
cues.zh: 具有液體般混亂結構的固體 其中的分子可自由移動 填充任何的間隙

cues.text: This makes the surface of glass uniform on a microscopic level,
cues.en: This makes the surface of glass uniform on a microscopic level,
cues.zh: 這使玻璃表面 即使由微觀的角度看來 也是平整的 因此光線照射上去

cues.text: allowing light to strike it without being scattered in different directions.
cues.en: allowing light to strike it without being scattered in different directions.
cues.zh: 因此光線照射上去 也不會四處散射 但這仍然不能解釋

cues.text: But this still doesn't explain why light is able to pass through glass
cues.en: But this still doesn't explain why light is able to pass through glass
cues.zh: 但這仍然不能解釋 為何光線能夠穿透玻璃

cues.text: rather than being absorbed as with most solids.
cues.en: rather than being absorbed as with most solids.
cues.zh: 為何光線能夠穿透玻璃 而不是像其他固體一樣被吸收

cues.text: For that, we need to go all the way down to the subatomic level.
cues.en: For that, we need to go all the way down to the subatomic level.
cues.zh: 為此，我們得進入 原子內的世界來瞭解 你可能知道 一個原子的組成包含一個原子核

cues.text: You may know that an atom consists of a nucleus with electrons orbiting around it,
cues.en: You may know that an atom consists of a nucleus with electrons orbiting around it,
cues.zh: 你可能知道 一個原子的組成包含一個原子核 以及若干圍繞在周圍的電子

cues.text: but you may be surprised to know that it's mostly empty space.
cues.en: but you may be surprised to know that it's mostly empty space.
cues.zh: 以及若干圍繞在周圍的電子 但你可能會很驚訝地發現 原子裡大部分是空蕩蕩的 事實上，如果將原子 比喻成一個體育場這麼大

cues.text: In fact, if an atom were the size of a sports stadium, the nucleus would be like a single pea in the center,
cues.en: In fact, if an atom were the size of a sports stadium, the nucleus would be like a single pea in the center,
cues.zh: 事實上，如果將原子 比喻成一個體育場這麼大 原子核就像是一顆在場中央的豌豆 而電子便是

cues.text: while the electrons would be like grains of sand in the outer seats.
cues.en: while the electrons would be like grains of sand in the outer seats.
cues.zh: 而電子便是 在場外圍座位的砂粒

cues.text: That should leave plenty of space for light to pass through without hitting any of these particles.
cues.en: That should leave plenty of space for light to pass through without hitting any of these particles.
cues.zh: 在場外圍座位的砂粒 因此 光線有大量的空間能夠穿透 而不會撞擊到這些粒子

cues.text: So the real question is not why is glass transparent, but why aren't all materials transparent?
cues.en: So the real question is not why is glass transparent, but why aren't all materials transparent?
cues.zh: 所以真正的問題並不是 為什麼玻璃是透明的 而是為什麼其他的材料不是透明的？ 這個問題的答案

cues.text: The answer has to do with the different energy levels that electrons in an atom can have.
cues.en: The answer has to do with the different energy levels that electrons in an atom can have.
cues.zh: 這個問題的答案 與原子內的電子 具有不同程度的能量有關 你可以把它想成是體育場裡

cues.text: Think of these as different rows of seats in the stadium stands.
cues.en: Think of these as different rows of seats in the stadium stands.
cues.zh: 與原子內的電子 具有不同程度的能量有關 你可以把它想成是體育場裡 一排排的座位

cues.text: An electron is initially assigned to sit in a certain row, but it could jump to a better row,
cues.en: An electron is initially assigned to sit in a certain row, but it could jump to a better row,
cues.zh: 一開始，一顆電子 被指定坐在某一排 但若是它有足夠的能量

cues.text: if it only had the energy.
cues.en: if it only had the energy.
cues.zh: 但若是它有足夠的能量 就可以跳到比較好的座位

cues.text: As luck would have it, absorbing one of those light photons passing through the atom can provide
cues.en: As luck would have it, absorbing one of those light photons passing through the atom can provide
cues.zh: 如果幸運的話 吸收穿過原子的光子 正好可以提供 這個電子所需的能量

cues.text: just the energy the electron needs.
cues.en: just the energy the electron needs.
cues.zh: 這個電子所需的能量 不過還有一個問題

cues.text: But there's a catch.
cues.en: But there's a catch.
cues.zh: 這個電子所需的能量 不過還有一個問題

cues.text: The energy from the photon has to be the right amount to get an electron to the next row.
cues.en: The energy from the photon has to be the right amount to get an electron to the next row.
cues.zh: 不過還有一個問題 這個光子提供的能量 必須正好等於 把電子送到下一排所需的能量

cues.text: Otherwise, it will just let the photon pass by, and it just so happens that in glass,
cues.en: Otherwise, it will just let the photon pass by, and it just so happens that in glass,
cues.zh: 不然，電子就只得任由光子透過 這就恰如發生在玻璃當中 由於排與排之間相隔非常遙遠

cues.text: the rows are so far apart that a photon of visible light
cues.en: the rows are so far apart that a photon of visible light
cues.zh: 這就恰如發生在玻璃當中 由於排與排之間相隔非常遙遠 可見光的光子

cues.text: can't provide enough energy for an electron to jump between them.
cues.en: can't provide enough energy for an electron to jump between them.
cues.zh: 無法提供電子足夠的能量 在排與排之間跳躍 另一方面，紫外線的光子

cues.text: Photons from ultraviolet light, on the other hand, give just the right amount of energy,
cues.en: Photons from ultraviolet light, on the other hand, give just the right amount of energy,
cues.zh: 在排與排之間跳躍 另一方面，紫外線的光子 便提供恰恰好的能量

cues.text: and are absorbed, which is why you can't get a suntan through glass.
cues.en: and are absorbed, which is why you can't get a suntan through glass.
cues.zh: 便提供恰恰好的能量 而被吸收 這就是為什麼隔著玻璃 皮膚不會被曬黑的原因

cues.text: This amazing property of being both solid and transparent has given glass many uses
cues.en: This amazing property of being both solid and transparent has given glass many uses
cues.zh: 玻璃這種兼具堅固而透明 令人驚歎的特質 賦予了玻璃多種用途

cues.text: throughout the centuries.
cues.en: throughout the centuries.
cues.zh: 令人驚歎的特質 賦予了玻璃多種用途 達數世紀之久

cues.text: From windows that let in light while keeping out the elements, to lenses that allow us to see both
cues.en: From windows that let in light while keeping out the elements, to lenses that allow us to see both
cues.zh: 達數世紀之久 從能透入光線 卻將其他元素阻隔在外的窗戶 到能讓我們看到

cues.text: the vast worlds beyond our planet, and the tiny ones right around us.
cues.en: the vast worlds beyond our planet, and the tiny ones right around us.
cues.zh: 地球以外的浩瀚世界 以及我們週遭的渺小事物

cues.text: It is hard to imagine modern civilization without glass.
cues.en: It is hard to imagine modern civilization without glass.
cues.zh: 實在很難想像 沒有玻璃的現代文明 對於玻璃這麼重要的一個物質

cues.text: And yet for such an important material we rarely think about glass and its impact.
cues.en: And yet for such an important material we rarely think about glass and its impact.
cues.zh: 對於玻璃這麼重要的一個物質 我們卻鮮少想到它及其影響 就是因為玻璃最重要的

cues.text: It is precisely because the most important and useful quality of glass is
cues.en: It is precisely because the most important and useful quality of glass is
cues.zh: 就是因為玻璃最重要的 也最有用的特質就是 平凡而且看不見

cues.text: being featureless and invisible that we often forget that it's even there.
cues.en: being featureless and invisible that we often forget that it's even there.
cues.zh: 平凡而且看不見 所以我們常常忘記它的存在
